 Economic Security Is a Disability Policy Issue 
 November 1, 2026 / Disability Belongs® Staff 
 Economic Security Is a Disability Policy Issue 
 The numbers highlight the scale of the challenge. In 2024,  23.6%  of disabled adults ages 18 to 64 living in the community were living in poverty, compared with 9.6% of adults without disabilities in the same age group, according to Census Bureau data analyzed by the Center for Research on Disability. In 2025, the employment-population ratio for people with disabilities ages 16 to 64 was  38.1% , compared with 74.8% for people without disabilities, according to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.
 Public policy can either help address these disparities or make them harder to overcome. For example, Supplemental Security Income (SSI), which millions of low-income people with disabilities and older adults receive each month, limits countable resources to  $2,000  for individuals and $3,000 for couples, thresholds unchanged since 1989. These limits can make saving for emergencies or the future difficult for people who depend on essential benefits.
 SSI rules can also create financial penalties for marriage. When two people receiving SSI marry, their combined maximum benefit is lower than the total they could receive as two individuals. When someone receiving SSI marries a person who does not receive SSI, their spouse’s income and resources may also be counted when determining their eligibility and benefit amount. These rules can force disabled people to make difficult financial choices about their relationships and futures.
 Disability Belongs® advocates for policy changes that address these barriers, from eliminating outdated asset limits and marriage penalties to ending subminimum wage and expanding employment opportunities. We also advocate for sustained funding for the programs and services people with disabilities rely on to live and participate in their communities.
 Government should work for the people it serves, and having a voice in how decisions are made should not be limited to those in positions of power. When organizations like Disability Belongs® bring disabled people’s experiences and priorities to policymakers, we help make sure those voices are heard and push for policies that better reflect our community’s needs.
 Explore our  Policy Agenda  to learn what we’re advocating for and how we’re working to advance economic security, independence, and opportunity for people with disabilities.

 Disability Belongs® is a diverse, disability-led nonprofit dedicated to changing how society views and values people with disabilities. By redefining narratives of disability, developing disability-inclusive leaders, and driving opportunity for the disability community, Disability Belongs® empowers people to thrive in all aspects of life.

 Disability Belongs® is a diverse, disability-led nonprofit that works to create systemic change in how society views and values people with disabilities, and that advances policies and practices that empower people with disabilities to have a better future. Our mission is to drive cultural and policy change to ensure our full representation and influence, creating a more accessible, equitable, and inclusive society.
